contexts.text: The Lord's Church is compared to... the seasons; its first age, to the Spring, when all things blossom; and the one preceding its last, to the Autumn, when they begin to grow inert.
When a man who had lived in good is let back into his proprium... there then appears as it were an inundation... this state is the evening, or autumn, of Spirits.
(The ideas of autumn and evening are, with the Angels, turned into the idea of love and wisdom as they are in their third state with them.)
The good which has been taken away, on account of which there is lamentation, is meant by the fruits of autumn ().
By the fruits of autumn are signified the goods of the Church...
